analysis:
The Congress's 2009 Lok Sabha manifesto promised to bring a strong Lokpal to curb corruption.

The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011 was passed by Parliament on 17 December 2013 and the Act received the President's assent on 1 January 2014, inside the UPA-II term. The January 2014 Act followed the 2011 anti-corruption movement led by Anna Hazare, whose supporters and several parties argued the enacted version was weaker than the draft Jan Lokpal Bill.

The Lokpal institution itself was not constituted until 19 March 2019, when its first chairperson and members were appointed. As of the end of the INC era in May 2014, the enabling law existed but the ombudsman was not operational.
